nodes.title: Barnes G-function
nodes.statement: The Barnes G-function is the entire function G : ℂ → ℂ given by the Weierstrass product G(z + 1) = (2π)^{z/2} exp(−z(z + 1)/2 − γ z²/2) Π_{k≥1} (1 + z/k)^k exp(−z + z²/(2k)), with γ Euler’s constant. It satisfies G(z + 1) = Γ(z) G(z) and G(1) = 1, its zeros are at z = −n (n ≥ 0) with multiplicity n + 1, and as z → ∞ in |ph z| ≤ π − δ, Ln G(z + 1) has the asymptotic expansion z²/4 + z Ln Γ(z + 1) − (z(z + 1)/2 + 1/12) ln z − ln A + Σ_{k≥1} B_{2k+2}/(2k(2k+1)(2k+2) z^{2k}), with A Glaisher’s constant.
hypotheses: Logarithms are principal on the positive real axis and continued by continuity (DLMF §4.2(i)).
proofSteps: Define G(z + 1) by the product; the k-th factor is 1 + O(|z|³/k²) on compact sets, so the product converges locally uniformly to an entire function, with the stated zeros.
Compare the logarithmic derivatives of G(z + 2)/G(z + 1) and of Γ(z + 1) through the Weierstrass product of 1/Γ; they agree, and the values at z = 0 fix G(z + 1) = Γ(z) G(z).
The integral formula Ln G(z + 1) = z ln(2π)/2 − z(z + 1)/2 + z Ln Γ(z + 1) − ∫₀^z Ln Γ(t + 1) dt (DLMF 5.17.4) and the Stirling series give the asymptotic expansion.

uses.how: the identity contribution of the Selberg trace formula is a power of Γ(s)/G(s + 1)² times elementary factors
the gamma-type factor of the compact Selberg functional equation
poles and zeros of the identity factor

gaps.detail: Fix g≥1. Let E be any degree2g CM field, L its normal closure over Q (not an arbitrary Galois overfield), G=Gal(L/Q), and c the central complex conjugation. Let F(E) be the finite set of isomorphism classes of nontrivial irreducible complex G-representations ρ satisfying ρ(c)=−Id. Then |G|≤M_g=(2g)!, |F(E)|≤M_g and dim ρ≤M_g. All constants below are uniform in E and ρ∈F(E). The CM owner proves that the nontrivial factors in the averaged Colmez expression belong to this family and that their rational coefficients have absolute value≤B_g; the trivial factor is separated before evaluation at1. For each ρ∈F(E), import an integral monomial Brauer expression χ_ρ=Σ_(j∈J)n_j Ind_(H_j)^G ψ_j with one-dimensional finite-order ψ_j, Σ_j|n_j|≤B_g, |J|≤B_g and [L^(H_j):Q]≤M_g. Bound each Hecke analytic conductor (including the base-field discriminant) by D_E^C_g, with D_E=|Disc(E)|. For δ_j=1 if ψ_j is trivial and0 otherwise, take the holomorphic, nonzero extension H_j(s) of (s−1)^δ_j L(s,ψ_j) at1. Prove Σ_j n_jδ_j=0 and the local germ identity L(s,ρ)=∏_j H_j(s)^n_j. The exact CM coefficient export is assigned to the extraction’s proposed quantitative CM PartII, whose stage does not yet exist. General Artin conductors belong to the proposed ArtinRepresentations supplier identified by current NFA, not NFA’s permutation-only formula. sourceIssues.locator: Published §I.2 conditions(i)–(iii), p.212; transform and reflected-contour proof p.213

sourceIssues.reason: Take c=0, ε=1/4 and F(x)=exp(x/4) for x<0, exp(−2x) for x≥0, F(0)=1. The printed weighted function is exp(x) on x<0 and exp(−5x/4) on x≥0, integrable/BV and continuous. sourceIssues.locator: §4, proof of Proposition 18, formula (7), p. 433 (PDF p. 23 of the author-hosted scan of the published article)
sourceIssues.printed: It defines t_{n,m,γ} = (nm)^{−1/2} e_X, where the matrix [1 γ; 0 n/m] represents the double class X.
sourceIssues.correction: X = double class of [1 γ/m; 0 n/m]. For m = 1 the printed formula is right.
sourceIssues.reason: By the paper's own formulas (1), (3) and (4), (e(γ) ∗ e_{X_m⁻¹})(g) = e_{X_m⁻¹}([1 −γ; 0 1]g), and for g = [1 b; 0 a] the argument [1, b − γa; 0, a] lies in the double class of [1 0; 0 1/m] exactly when a = 1/m and b ∈ γ/m + (1/m)ℤ. So e(γ)μ*_m = m^{−1/2}e_X with X the class of [1 γ/m; 0 1/m], and left multiplication by μ_n multiplies the (2,2) entry by n. The double class of [1 b; 0 n/m] depends only on b mod (1/m)ℤ, so as printed t_{1,2,1/2} = t_{1,2,0} = μ*_2. But e(1/2)μ*_2 = μ*_2 is impossible: its adjoint μ_2 e(−1/2) = μ_2, multiplied on the left by μ*_2, gives e(−1/2) = 1 by relation (a). With the corrected entry, (n, m, γ) ↦ X is a bijection onto the double cosets, which is the linear independence the proof asserts next.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform prime-power divisor bound
proofDependencies.statement: For ε>0, integers p≥2 and a≥0, put D=max(1,(ε log 2)⁻¹). Then a+1≤D p^(aε). D is notation for a real expression, not a new carrier.
hypotheses: ε>0; p,a natural; p≥2
proofSketch: Logarithm monotonicity gives log p≥log 2>0. Thus D≥1 and D ε log p≥1.
Multiply the latter inequality by a≥0 and add 1≤D to obtain a+1≤D(1+aε log p).
Use 1+t≤exp t and p^(aε)=exp(aε log p).

locators.locator: Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split

proofDependencies.title: Large-prime divisor factor bound
proofDependencies.statement: For ε>0, positive integer p and a≥0, exp(1/ε)≤p implies a+1≤p^(aε).
hypotheses: ε>0; p>0; a natural; exp(1/ε)≤p
proofSketch: Apply the exponential/logarithm equivalence to get ε log p≥1.
Multiply by a, add 1 and apply 1+t≤exp t; identify the real power.

locators.locator: Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split

proofDependencies.title: Divisor bounds from local factors
proofDependencies.statement: Let ε∈ℝ, D≥1 and B∈ℕ. Suppose for every prime p and a∈ℕ that a+1≤D p^(aε) if p≤B, and a+1≤p^(aε) if p>B. For every n>0, τ(n)≤D^B n^ε, with τ(n)=card(n.divisors).
hypotheses: D≥1; B natural; two uniform prime-power hypotheses; n>0
proofSketch: Use Nat.card_divisors to write τ(n)=∏p|n(a_p+1); use Nat.prod_primeFactors_pow_factorization to write n=∏p|n p^a_p.
Split the finite prime-factor set at p≤B. Multiply the respective nonnegative local bounds using Finset.prod_le_prod.
Repeated Real.mul_rpow and Real.rpow_mul identify the prime-power product with n^ε. At most B small prime divisors occur, since they inject into {1,…,B}.
Hence τ(n)≤D^r n^ε with r≤B; D≥1 gives D^r≤D^B.

locators.locator: Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split

proofDependencies.title: Absorption of the divisor-bound constant
proofDependencies.statement: For n>0 and ε,δ,C∈ℝ, if τ(n)≤C n^ε and C≤n^(δ−ε), then τ(n)≤n^δ.
hypotheses: n>0; the two displayed inequalities
proofSketch: Multiply C≤n^(δ−ε) by n^ε≥0 and compose with the first inequality.
Apply Real.rpow_add at positive n and simplify (δ−ε)+ε=δ.

locators.locator: Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split

proofDependencies.title: Ray-class product has no boundary zeros
proofDependencies.statement: For the finite character group of a ray class quotient, the product of the continued Hecke L-functions has no zeros at regular points of Re s≥1. At s=1 it has meromorphic order ≤0, permitting the principal-character pole. Each Euler logarithmic coefficient is nonnegative by finite-character orthogonality, with bad-prime factors treated separately.
hypotheses: K a number field; 𝔪 a modulus (an integral ideal times a set of real places); χ a character of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(K) (finite order), identified with a finite-order idele-class character ω_χ by GlobalNumberFields Layer 9; L(s, χ) = Σ_{(𝔞,𝔪)=1} χ(𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} for Re s > 1.
proofSketch: Expand the logarithm of the convergent Euler products on Re s>1.
Use finite-character orthogonality, separately planned below, to obtain nonnegative coefficients.
Apply the Hecke boundary adapter with the single principal-character pole and holomorphy of every other factor.

proofDependencies.title: Gluing m-th roots across the line Re s = 1
proofDependencies.statement: Let f be holomorphic and zero-free on {Re s > 1}, m ≥ 1, and U an open set containing {Re s = 1} ∖ {1} on which a holomorphic, zero-free g is given with g = f^m on U ∩ {Re s > 1}. Then f extends holomorphically (and zero-free) to {Re s > 1} ∪ U′ for an open U′ ⊇ {Re s = 1} ∖ {1}: on each disc D ⊆ U centred on the line there is a unique holomorphic h_D with h_D^m = g agreeing with f on the connected set D ∩ {Re s > 1}, and the h_D agree on overlaps.
hypotheses: Discs D centred at points of Re s = 1 with D ⊆ U; D ∩ {Re s > 1} is a nonempty half-disc, hence connected.
proofSketch: On the simply connected D, g has m holomorphic m-th roots, differing by m-th roots of unity; exactly one agrees with f at a point of D ∩ {Re s > 1}, hence on all of it (identity theorem on the connected half-disc).
On D ∩ D′ ∩ {Re s > 1} ≠ ∅ both roots equal f, so they agree on the connected D ∩ D′ (a lens, connected) by the identity theorem.

proofDependencies.title: Quadratic Hecke value as residue quotient
proofDependencies.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F, L_f(1,η)=κ_E/κ_F>0, where κ_K is the positive residue of the continued Dedekind function. Here η is the canonical nontrivial primitive quadratic Hecke character attached by global Artin reciprocity. Its holomorphy at 1, the continued zeta factorization, and the two simple positive residues give the quotient; general line-one nonvanishing is not needed for this argument.
proofSketch: Multiply the continued quadratic factorization by s−1 and take the limit at 1.
Cancel the positive κ_F and use holomorphy of the nonprincipal Hecke factor.

locators.locator: Quadratic Euler-factor calculation; Thorner-Zaman 2017 equations (2-1)-(2-7); main Corollary 3.3 adapter

proofDependencies.title: Integrated prime-divisor mean
proofDependencies.statement: With a,C as in the prime-divisor mean lemma, ∫_0^T Σ_{1≤t≤x}a(t)dx=Σ_{1≤t≤T}(T−t)a(t)=CT²/2+O_{n,c}(T^(3/2)), T≥1.
proofSketch: For every t≥1 integrate its indicator over 0≤x≤T: the integral is T−t when t≤T and zero otherwise. Interchange only the finitely many nonzero terms.
Integrate the mean estimate on [1,T]; on [0,1) the count is zero and the integral of Cx is bounded by a constant depending only on n,c. The remainder integral is at most a fixed multiple of T^(3/2).

proofDependencies.title: Two-sided error and the zero term
proofDependencies.statement: For y,z≥2 and A>0 the two-sided sum Σ_{|r|≤y}E_z(r)e^(irα) has absolute value ≤2C_A y(log y)(log z)^−A+|E_z(0)|. The zero term is bounded separately by O_A(z(log z)^−A).
proofSketch: Pair the positive and negative summands using evenness; apply the positive estimate to α and −α.
Use Möbius cancellation and partial summation for the finite zero sum.

proofDependencies.title: Isolate the origin zero
proofDependencies.statement: For nonzero entire f, with m=analyticOrderNatAt f 0, there is an entire g with g(0)≠0 and f(z)=z^m g(z) for all z. If f has order at most ρ≥0, so does g.
proofSketch: Entirety and the identity theorem exclude a locally zero germ. The finite analytic-order factorization gives a local analytic g with g(0)≠0.

Define g(z)=f(z)/z^m off zero and use that local residual value at zero; equality to the analytic residual on a neighbourhood patches the quotient analytically. No unverified global removable-singularity theorem is required.
For |z|≥1 division by z^m cannot increase the bound. Continuity bounds the remaining compact ball.

proofDependencies.title: Multiplicity count of compact zeros
proofDependencies.statement: A nonzero entire f has finitely many zeros in each closed disk, and every zero has finite analytic multiplicity.
proofSketch: The nonzero entire hypothesis and the identity theorem exclude a locally zero germ at every point; hence each analytic order is finite.

Apply the global isolated-zero/codiscrete theorem on C. Restrict its codiscrete nonzero set to a closed disk and apply the compact finite-complement theorem; sum the finitely many finite multiplicities.

proofDependencies.title: Zero count from an order bound
proofDependencies.statement: If g is entire, g(0)≠0 and has order at most ρ, then for every b>ρ the number n_g(r) of zeros with multiplicity in |z|≤r is O_b(r^b) for r≥1.
hypotheses: ρ≥0; g entire and g(0)≠0; orderAtMost(g,ρ); r≥1; zeros are counted with analytic multiplicity.
proofSketch: For b>ρ, enlarge the global growth constant so M=C_b exp((2r)^b)≥1. Apply the pinned Jensen inequality with centre 0, positive inner radius r and outer radius 2r.
The exact upper bound is log(M/|g(0)|)/log 2. It is bounded by K_{g,b}r^b for r≥1. Pinned Jensen permits zeros on the outer circle; its stated analytic-neighbourhood hypothesis holds by entirety.

proofDependencies.statement: For a nonzero entire g with g(0)≠0 and order at most one, its nonzero zero family α_i, with every index carrying one occurrence of analytic multiplicity, satisfies Σ_i|α_i|⁻²<∞. Finite and empty index sets are included.
proofSketch: Choose b=3/2 in the Jensen zero count.
Split |α|≥1 into dyadic annuli; their contributions are bounded by C·2^(−j/2). Handle the finitely many inner zeros separately.

proofDependencies.title: Small canonical-factor logarithm
proofDependencies.statement: On |w|≤1/2 set L(w)=Log(1−w)+w, using the principal logarithm. This is the analytic logarithm of E₁(w) with L(0)=0: exp L(w)=E₁(w), L(w)=−Σ_{k≥2}w^k/k, and |L(w)|≤|w|². The logarithm series and its numerical remainder estimate are imported pinned results, not new versions of those general results.
proofSketch: For |w|≤1/2, 1−w lies in the slit plane. Its principal logarithm is analytic and exp(Log(1−w)+w)=(1−w)exp(w).
Subtract the n=0 and n=1 terms from the pinned HasSum logarithm expansion. Substitute z=−w in the pinned remainder estimate and use 2(1−|w|)≥1.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform tail bound for the canonical product
proofDependencies.statement: Under the stated family hypotheses, for R>0 the log-factor tails Σ_{i in S, |α_i|>2R}(Log(1−z/α_i)+z/α_i), directed by finite subsets S, converge uniformly for |z|≤R. Every omitted-tail norm is at most R² times the corresponding reciprocal-square tail.

proofSketch: Use the small-factor logarithm bound and dominate every tail by R²Σ_tail |α|^−2.
Keep the finite inner factors outside the logarithm to allow zeros inside the disk.

P is entire and P(0)=1. Enumeration changes preserve this product; finite and empty families are included.
hypotheses: An indexed family α_i of nonzero complex numbers; every bounded disk contains finitely many indices, with repeated values representing multiplicity; Σ_i|α_i|⁻²<∞.
proofSketch: Exponentiate the uniformly convergent logarithmic tail and multiply by the finite inner factors.
Apply the pinned locally uniform holomorphic-limit theorem.

proofDependencies.title: Analyticity of a continuous logarithm
proofDependencies.statement: If g is analytic and nonzero on open U, and a continuous L satisfies exp(L)=g on U, then L is analytic on U.
proofSketch: For x∈U, shrink to a neighbourhood where g(y)/g(x) lies near 1 in the slit plane. Define the analytic local lift ℓ(y)=L(x)+Log(g(y)/g(x)); then exp ℓ=g and ℓ(x)=L(x).

By the pinned exponential-kernel theorem L(y)−ℓ(y) is an integer multiple of 2πi. Continuity makes its norm <2π on a smaller neighbourhood, where it must be zero. Thus L locally equals the analytic ℓ, with no simply connected hypothesis on U.

proofDependencies.statement: If forbidden intervals around |α| have total length at most M<∞, then every [r,r+M+1] contains a radius not in their union.
proofSketch: The interval has length M+1, while the union has outer length≤M.
Consequently the good radii have bounded gaps, not merely a subsequence tending to infinity.

proofDependencies.statement: For every 0<ε<1 there is C_ε>0 such that every good radius R≥2 satisfying |R−|α_i||>|α_i|⁻² for all i obeys log|P(z)|≥−C_ε R^(1+ε) for every |z|=R. Every [r,r+M+1] with r≥2 contains such a radius, where M=2Σ_i|α_i|⁻²; thus the good radii have bounded gaps.

P is its genus-one unordered canonical product, including finite/empty families.
proofSketch: Choose b=1+ε/2, and fix its zero-count constant before R. Split factors into |α_i|<R/2, R/2≤|α_i|≤2R and |α_i|>2R.

Apply the three named inner/middle/outer lower-bound lemmas. The first two factors are finite and nonzero; the outer factor is a nonzero exponential. Their product is P by finite/infinite product splitting.

Use 1+log(2R)≤K_ε R^(ε/2) for R≥2 to absorb the middle range and add the bounds. Each forbidden closed interval has length 2|α_i|⁻²; summable-excluded-radii supplies a good radius in every interval of length M+1.

At an arbitrary centre c, the same global bound on radius R is at most K_{c,ε}(1+R^(1+ε)) for R≥max(1,|c|). Apply the pinned second-derivative Cauchy estimate and let R tend to infinity. The upper bound tends to zero, so h″ vanishes everywhere and h is affine.

proofSketch: Use the canonical-product compact-tail estimate to prove summability of the regularized derivative summands on each compact set avoiding the zero family.

proofDependencies.statement: Under these hypotheses, there is c>0 and a locally finite positive-real family λ_j, with one index per positive-imaginary zero occurrence, such that f(z)=c z^m∏_j(1+z²/λ_j²). The products converge locally uniformly over finite subsets; finite and empty families are included.
hypotheses: f entire and not identically zero; m is its finite analytic order at zero; orderAtMost(f,1); f(−z)=(−1)^m f(z); every zero is purely imaginary; f(x) is positive real for all sufficiently large positive real x.
proofSketch: Parity gives equal zero multiplicities at ±iλ. Pair the genus-one factors by canonical-factor-pair; reciprocal-square summability makes this reindexing valid.

The paired product is even and has value 1 at zero. Comparing f(−z) and (−1)^m f(z) near zero gives exp(−2bz)=1 for all sufficiently small z, forcing b=0. For positive x every paired factor and x^m is positive, so eventual positive reality of f forces c=exp(a)>0.

proofDependencies.title: Exponential decay of the theta tail
proofDependencies.statement: For x≥1, ω(x)=(HurwitzZeta.evenKernel(0,x)−1)/2=Σ_(n≥1)exp(−πn²x) satisfies 0≤ω(x)≤exp(−πx)/(1−exp(−π)); reuse the existing theta kernel.
proofSketch: Pair n and -n in the pinned integer Gaussian HasSum at a=0, retaining its n=0 term1, to identify the positive-natural theta tail.
For n≥1 and x≥1, n²−1≥n−1, so exp(−πn²x)≤exp(−πx)exp(−π(n−1)).
Sum the nonnegative geometric majorant. Its ratio exp(−π) lies strictly between0 and1, including the endpoint x=1.

proofDependencies.title: Entire integral representation of xi
proofDependencies.statement: For all s∈C, ξ(s)=1/2+(1/2)s(s−1)∫_1^∞(x^(s/2−1)+x^((1−s)/2−1))ω(x)dx, where ω(x)=(HurwitzZeta.evenKernel(0,x)−1)/2. The integrand is absolutely integrable, and finite integrals up to R converge locally uniformly in s as R→∞.
proofSketch: Unfold completed0 as the zero-parameter Hurwitz weak-FE Mellin transform, not as a new meromorphic continuation of zeta.

Split the modified Mellin integral at1; its value at1 is measure zero. On x>1 the modified kernel is theta−1=2ω; on0<x<1 use the same weak-FE symmetry and substitution x=1/y to obtain the second x>1 integral.
On a compact set of s, each complex power and each s derivative is bounded by a fixed real power of x times a logarithmic power; exponential theta decay gives integrable domination.

Match the exact split/inversion, integrability and locally uniform truncated-integral declarations at the pin; these formal adapters remain in the gap ledger, not an assumed existing integral theorem.

proofDependencies.title: Growth bound for the theta integral
proofDependencies.statement: For every real r≥2, ∫_1^∞(x^(r/2+1)+1)exp(−πx)dx≤exp(2r log(2+r)). In particular one absolute growth constant works for all r; no Stirling theorem is required.
proofSketch: Set k=ceil(r/2+1), a natural integer. For r≥2, r/2+1≤k≤r/2+2≤r+1.
On x≥1, x^(r/2+1)≤x^k and exp(−πx)≤exp(−x). Extend both nonnegative integrals to x>0. Pinned gamma integrability and Gamma(k+1)=k! bound the sum by k!+1.
Use Nat.factorial_le_pow and real monotonicity to get k!+1≤2(r+1)^(r+1). Taking logarithms bounds this by exp(2r log(2+r)) for r≥2.
Keep integrability separate from the totalized integral value. This repairs the false uniform-in-x majorant in Lemma8.3.

proofDependencies.title: Order-one growth of xi
proofDependencies.statement: There are absolute C,R>0 such that |ξ(s)|≤exp(C|s|log(2+|s|)) for |s|≥R; consequently ξ has order at most1.
proofSketch: For r=|s|≥2 and x≥1, each complex power has norm x to its real exponent, bounded by x^(r/2+1)+1 after harmless enlargement.
Use the exponential theta bound and the explicit integral majorant; |s(s−1)|≤r(r+1). Absorb this polynomial and the absolute theta constant into exp(Cr log(2+r)).

For each b>1, log(2+r)=o(r^(b−1)), so the displayed growth is at most a constant times exp(r^b) for large r. Enlarge the constant on a compact disk and use xi entirety to obtain entire_order_at_most ξ1.

proofDependencies.title: Corrected logarithmic derivative of zeta
proofDependencies.statement: For s≠0,1 with ζ(s)≠0 and s/2 not a nonpositive integer, there exist Hadamard constants A,B and a locally finite multiplicity-indexed family of nonzero ξ zeros ρ such that ζ′(s)/ζ(s)=B−1/s−1/(s−1)+(log π)/2−(1/2)Γ′(s/2)/Γ(s/2)+Σ_ρ(1/(s−ρ)+1/ρ). The corrected sum is locally uniformly convergent away from ξ zeros.
proofSketch: Apply order-one Hadamard to the nonzero entire xi; ξ(0)=1/2 implies origin order0.
On the stated comparison domain, Gamma(s/2), s, s−1 and π^(−s/2) are all nonzero. Differentiate the xi product comparison and divide only there.
Use the derivative-limit theorem for the multiplicity-indexed canonical product; the regularized summand is s/(ρ(s−ρ)).
Equivalently combine the −1/s term with −(1/2)ψΓ(s/2) using ψΓ(z+1)=ψΓ(z)+1/z; this yields ψΓ(1+s/2), never the printed ψΓ((s+1)/2).

proofDependencies.title: Logarithmic gamma bound
proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for every complex z with Re z≥1/2 and |z|≥2, |Complex.digamma(z)−Log(z)|≤C/|z|; the logarithm is principal. Consequently |Γ′(z)/Γ(z)|≤C′log(2+|z|) with an absolute C′.
proofSketch: Use the existing digamma=logDeriv Gamma carrier and pinned Gamma nonvanishing for positive real part.
DLMF5.11.2 and §5.11(ii) give the sector-uniform remainder after Log z−1/(2z); on |arg z|≤π/2 its sec(arg z/2)^3 factor is bounded. This supplies an explicit first-remainder target.
An asymptotic statement alone is not a formal proof adapter. Read the underlying complex Euler–Maclaurin/Stirling remainder proof and match its constants and branch at the pin before closing the gap.
Bound |Log z|≤log|z|+π/2 on the right half-plane, absorbing the remainder into log(2+|z|).

proofDependencies.title: Bounded right-edge logarithmic derivative
proofDependencies.statement: For every complex s with Re s≥2, |ζ′(s)/ζ(s)|≤Σ_(n≥1)Λ(n)n^−2<∞, with the same absolute constant for every imaginary part.
proofSketch: Import the pinned absolute summability and identity of the complex von-Mangoldt L-series for Re s>1.
Use Λ(n)≥0 and the complex-power norm formula; for n≥1 and Re s≥2, n^(−Re s)≤n^−2.
Sum the termwise norm bound. Absolute convergence at s=2 is already the pinned summability theorem; do not re-plan its log n integral comparison.

proofDependencies.title: Pole term near one
proofDependencies.statement: There are absolute δ,K>0 such that for every real1<σ<1+δ, |−ζ′(σ)/ζ(σ)−1/(σ−1)|≤K.
proofSketch: Use the pinned regular-completion formula to construct the analytic pole-cleared germ g(s)=(s−1)ζ(s) off1, with g(1)=1. The punctured residue limit fixes this value; residue alone is not derivative control.
The regular denominator 2π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2+1) is analytic and nonzero near1. In the formula the numerator of g simplifies to 1+s(s−1)completed0(s).
Shrink the neighbourhood so g is nonzero and its logarithmic derivative is bounded on a compact disk. Off1, −ζ′/ζ=1/(s−1)−g′/g; restrict to the real right-hand interval.

proofDependencies.title: Zeta three-four-one inequality
proofDependencies.statement: For σ>1 and real t, 3(−ζ′/ζ)(σ)+4Re(−ζ′/ζ)(σ+it)+Re(−ζ′/ζ)(σ+2it)≥0.
proofSketch: Import ADS8’s nonnegative3-4-1 trigonometric package, retaining that upstream ownership.
Specialize the pinned absolutely convergent von-Mangoldt logarithmic-derivative series at σ,σ+it,σ+2it.
Each coefficient is Λ(n)n^−σ≥0; its bracket is3+4cos(t log n)+cos(2t log n)=2(1+cos(t log n))². Absolute summability permits taking real parts and adding the three series.

proofDependencies.title: A near-one zero forces a positive reciprocal term
proofDependencies.statement: For a ξ zero ρ=β+it and1<σ≤2, 0<β<1 and Re(1/(σ+it−ρ))=1/(σ−β)>0. For every other ξ zero ρ′, Re(1/(σ+it−ρ′))≥0 and Re(1/ρ′)>0. The real parts of the regularized Hadamard summands may therefore be dropped or bounded below by any one retained term.
proofSketch: First invoke xi-zero-critical-strip; its strict boundaries follow from pinned zeta nonvanishing and xi reflection, not from the zero-count definition.
For s=σ+it and ρ′=β′+it′, Re(1/(s−ρ′))=(σ−β′)/((σ−β′)²+(t−t′)²)>0. At ρ′=ρ this is1/(σ−β).
Also Re(1/ρ′)=β′/|ρ′|²>0. Reciprocal-square summability makes these nonnegative constant real parts summable, while local uniform convergence handles the full regularized sum.
Finite partial sums preserve the single-term lower bound; take their convergent limit to justify dropping the remaining terms.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform selection of the zero-free constant
proofDependencies.statement: There are effective absolute c>0 and t₀>1 such that any ξ zero β+it with t≥t₀ satisfies β<1−c/log t; hence the same high-height nontrivial zeta-zero exclusion holds.
proofSketch: On1<σ≤min(2,1+δ), |t|≥2, combine the corrected Hadamard formula with the gamma bound. The nonzero elementary rational terms are O(1) and gamma is O(log|t|), with constants uniform in σ.
Use positivity to obtain −Re ζ′/ζ(σ+2it)≤C log t and −Re ζ′/ζ(σ+it)≤C log t−1/(σ−β). Insert these and the real pole bound into the3-4-1 inequality, obtaining4/(σ−β)≤3/(σ−1)+C₀log t.
Enlarge C₀ to be at least1. Choose a=1/(2C₀), c=a/10. Then4/(a+c)>3/a+C₀. If β≥1−c/log t, set σ=1+a/log t and contradict the previous inequality.
Choose t₀ effectively so t₀≥2 and a/log t₀≤min(1,δ). Effective constants are conditional on an explicitly bounded gamma remainder and pole-germ radius; those outstanding adapters remain gaps.

proofDependencies.title: Local zero count
proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for every real T≥2, the number of nontrivial zeta-zero occurrences with T≤Imρ≤T+1 is at most C log(T+2).
proofSketch: Invoke zeta-poisson-zero-weight at t=T. Every zero in the closed unit interval has reciprocal-square weight≥1/2.
The xi/zeta API identifies analytic multiplicities inside the open critical strip; sum the finite nonnegative inequality.
For T≥2, log(T+2) is comparable to log T. This avoids the previously unverified shifted-Jensen centre lower bound and disk-growth estimate.

proofDependencies.title: Choosing a contour height
proofDependencies.statement: There are absolute c,C>0 such that for every T≥2 there is T′∈[T,T+1] with |T′−Imρ|≥c/log(T+2) for every ξ zeroρ. For x≥2, changing the symmetric strict cutoff from T to T′ changes Σmρ x^ρ/ρ by at most C x log(T+2)/T; arbitrary weights require their own uniform band bound.
proofSketch: Choose c small enough that h=c/log(T+2)≤1/4. Only ordinates in[T−1,T+2] can have excluded h-neighbourhoods meeting[T,T+1].
Cover this enlarged band by a fixed number of unit intervals; the positive-weight bound gives one C0 log(T+2) count, with multiplicity and bounded T included.
The total lengths of excluded closed intervals are at most2h C0 log(T+2). Choose c with this strictly less than1; finite interval subadditivity gives a point in[T,T+1] outside every interval.
Conjugation gives separation at−T′ too. Changed zero occurrences lie in the two unit bands; each |x^ρ/ρ|≤x/T. Add their finite count bound. No assertion is made for unbounded arbitrary weights.

proofDependencies.title: Local logarithmic-derivative expansion
proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for −1≤σ≤2,|t|≥2, and σ+it not a nontrivial zero, ζ′/ζ(σ+it)=Σ_(|t−Imρ|<1)mρ/(σ+it−ρ)+E(σ,t), with |E(σ,t)|≤C log(2+|t|). It also holds at a zero ordinate if the evaluation point itself is not a zero.
proofSketch: Subtract the corrected Hadamard formulas at s=σ+it and s0=2+it; the1/ρ corrections and B cancel.
Use digamma(z+1)=digamma(z)+1/z to move s/2 to1+s/2, whose real part is at least1/2. The gamma and elementary rational differences are O(log(2+|t|)); gamma poles and s=0,1 are absent because |t|≥2.
For |t−Imρ|≥1, the reciprocal difference is bounded in norm by3/|t−Imρ|²≤6/(1+(t−Imρ)²). The positive-weight lemma controls the entire tail, without an unproved separate annulus summation.
For |t−Imρ|<1, subtracting the s0 reciprocal costs at most1 per zero occurrence, because2−Reρ>1. Bound this local count with the same weight lemma; the pinned right-edge series controls ζ′/ζ(s0).

proofDependencies.title: Left-half-plane bound away from trivial zeros
proofDependencies.statement: For every fixed c>0 there is C_c>0 such that for every complex w with Re w≤−1 and |w+2n|≥c for every integer n≥1, ζ(w)≠0 and |ζ′(w)/ζ(w)|≤C_c log(2+|w|).
proofSketch: Set s=1−w, so Re s≥2. Import pinned riemannZeta_one_sub, already in the2(2π)^(-s)Gamma(s)cos(πs/2)zeta(s) form; no separate duplication/reflection construction is needed.
All factors are nonzero off the odd positive s integers, precisely the excluded negative-even w points. Differentiate the identity and divide on this regular domain.
The exponential factors contribute constants; digamma(s) is O(log(2+|s|)) and the pinned right-edge logarithmic zeta derivative is uniformly bounded.

The tangent factor is uniformly O_c(1): for large |Im s| use its exponential quotient; for bounded imaginary part use periodicity on a compact real strip avoiding cosine zeros by c. Bounded |s| is absorbed by compact continuity.

proofDependencies.title: Residues of the Perron integrand
proofDependencies.statement: For x>1, the integrand −(ζ′/ζ)(s)x^s/s has residue x at1, −m_ρx^ρ/ρ at a nontrivial zeroρ, x^(−2n)/(2n) at−2n, and −ζ′(0)/ζ(0) at0. Summing the trivial zeros gives −(1/2)log(1−x^−2).
proofSketch: At a nontrivial zeroρ of order mρ, write ζ(s)=(s−ρ)^mρ g(s), with analytic nonzero g; then −ζ′/ζ has residue−mρ. Multiplication by x^s/s evaluates the regular factor x^ρ/ρ.
At1 use the nonzero pole-cleared germ from zeta-pole-log-derivative; its logarithmic derivative gives the opposite residue+1, hence residue x.
Use zeta-trivial-zero-simple to obtain order1 at−2n, rather than merely importing a zero-value theorem. Its integrand residue is x^(−2n)/(2n).
At0, ζ(0)=−1/2 and zeta is analytic; only1/s contributes the residue−ζ′(0)/ζ(0). Sum the positive trivial-zero series using the convergent−log(1−u) Taylor series at u=x^−2∈(0,1).

Consume the completed ContourIntegration cycle residue theorem and current Tau Ceti classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous. Match the finite rectangle, winding numbers and local Laurent residues to its hypotheses; the zeta-specific adapter remains a gap, without re-planning the general theorem.

proofDependencies.title: Nearest-prime-power remainder
proofDependencies.statement: For real x≥2,T≥2,c=1+1/log x, put δ(x)=infDist(x,{m∈ℝ:m is a natural prime power and m≠x})>0. The Perron remainder for ψ₀(x), after retaining the exact endpoint kernel, is bounded by C[x log²(xT)/T+(log x)min(1,x/(Tδ(x)))], with one absolute C. A prime-power endpoint has half weight only in the infinite-height limit.
proofSketch: Prime powers are a nonempty locally finite subset of the positive integers. After excluding x, their distance has a positive attained minimum. The endpoint m=x is treated separately.
Use ADS6’s exact finite kernel. At y=1 its value is arctan(T/c)/π, and its difference from1/2 is O(c/T), contributing O(log x/T) here.

For |m/x−1|≥1/4, use the absolutely convergent Λ series and −ζ′(c)/ζ(c)=O(log x). The near-one pole estimate applies for sufficiently large x; for remaining x use positivity/summability at a fixed c>1 and compact absorption.
On each of the two intervals3x/4<m<x and x<m<5x/4, isolate the closest prime power. Its contribution is at most C log x min(1,x/(Tδ(x))).

For all other m in that interval use integer spacing, |log(m/x)|≥C|m−x|/x, Λ(m)≤log m and the positive harmonic sum. This contributes O(x log²x/T). The actual nearest-prime-power term remains unabsorbed.
Match the infDist/local-finiteness and finite-height kernel constants rather than assuming the formal infinite Perron identity can be summed absolutely.

proofDependencies.title: Horizontal contour bound
proofDependencies.statement: For x≥2, c=1+1/log x and a height T′≥2 separated from every ξ-zero ordinate by at least c₀/log(T′+2), the two horizontal Perron integrals from Re s=−1 to c have norm at most C_(c₀) x log²(T′+2)/(T′log x).
proofSketch: On−1≤σ≤min(2,c), the local expansion, unit count and height separation bound |ζ′/ζ(σ±iT′)| by C_(c0)log²(T′+2).
If2<c, use the pinned bounded right-edge series on the additional interval[2,c]. This case occurs for2≤x<e and was not covered by the previous local-expansion prerequisite alone.
On the entire segment |s|≥T′ and ∫_(−1)^c x^σ dσ=(x^c−x^−1)/log x≤e x/log x. Multiply the bounds and sum the two integrals.
For a good height from the selection lemma, c0 is fixed absolute, making C absolute.

proofDependencies.title: Left contour limit
proofDependencies.statement: For every fixed x≥2,T≥2, the Perron vertical integral at Re s=−U tends to0 as U→∞ through positive odd integers. Uniformly in x,T, the two horizontal tails Re s≤−1 have norm O(log(T+2)/(Tx log x)+1/(Tx(log x)²)), with an absolute constant.
proofSketch: For odd U, every point on the vertical segment remains distance≥1 from all negative-even trivial zeros. The left logarithmic-derivative bound gives norm at most C T log(2+U+T)/(U x^U), which tends to0 with x,T fixed.
On the two horizontal tails, |s|≥T and distance to every real trivial zero≥T≥2, so the same left bound has one absolute constant.
Use log(2+u+T)≤log(T+2)+u for u≥1, and integrate x^(−u) and u x^(−u) from1 to∞. Their exact values give the two displayed tail terms after absorbing1/log x in the log(T+2) term.
The limit is U→∞, correcting the source’s printed U→0 slip. No uniform limit over growing T is asserted.

proofDependencies.title: Low-zero-safe interval kernel
proofDependencies.statement: For every real x≥2 and complex ρ with0<Reρ<1, |(x^ρ−(x/2)^ρ)/ρ|≤2x^(Reρ)min(1,1/|ρ|). Positive-real powers use exp(ρ log x); the bound remains finite as ρ approaches0.
proofSketch: Since Reρ>0,ρ≠0. Integrate the derivative of t↦t^ρ on[x/2,x] to write the quotient as∫ t^(ρ−1)dt.
For t in that interval, t^(Reρ)≤x^(Reρ), so the integral norm is at most x^(Reρ)∫dt/t=x^(Reρ)log2.
The direct numerator bound is at most2x^(Reρ)/|ρ|. If |ρ|≤1 use log2≤2; if |ρ|≥1 use the second bound, yielding the explicit constant2.
The limit asρ→0 is log2, not a divergent reciprocal. The subtraction must precede absolute values.

proofDependencies.title: Logarithmic-square sum of zero weights
proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for every primitive Dirichlet characterχ of conductor q≥1 and every T≥2, Σ_(nontrivial zeros |Imρ|≤T)mρ min(1,1/|ρ|)≤C log²(q(T+2)). Nontrivial means0<Reρ<1, and multiplicity is analytic order.
proofSketch: For a primitive nonprincipal character, invoke the new conductor-uniform local count, including |Imρ|≤1; the weight there is at most1, so an arbitrarily low exceptional zero does not introduce1/|ρ|.
For each unit band m≤|Imρ|<m+1 with m≥1, the weight is at most1/m and the count is at most C0 log(q(m+2)).
Sum C0 log(q(m+2))/m for1≤m≤ceil T; the harmonic/log-harmonic bound is O(log q log(T+2)+log²(T+2)), at most O(log²(q(T+2))).
The primitive principal conductor1 case is the zeta-only count from zeta-poisson-zero-weight and the same band argument.
The original conductor-uniform local proof remains unread; the summation deduction is explicit and does not license the false unweighted1/|ρ| estimate at tiny zeros.

proofDependencies.title: Direct sums of Artin local factors
proofDependencies.statement: For ρ₁,ρ₂, P_p(ρ₁⊕ρ₂,T)=P_p(ρ₁,T)P_p(ρ₂,T) at every prime, including ramified primes. Hence L(ρ₁⊕ρ₂)=L(ρ₁)L(ρ₂) on Re s>1.
proofSketch: The inertia-fixed subspace of the direct sum is the direct sum of fixed subspaces by the existing invariants membership formula. Transport Frobenius to the block diagonal map.
Apply LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap to the two finite endomorphisms and transport through polynomial reversal, or use the corresponding determinant block identity.
Use node162 absolute local uniform convergence to multiply the finite local identities in the directed limit of prime sets; no statement about arbitrary totalized products is used.

proofDependencies.title: Absolute convergence of Artin factors
proofDependencies.statement: For fixed dimension d and ε>0, uniformly on Re s≥1+ε, the local factors satisfy |P_p((Np)^−s)^−1−1|≤C_{d,ε}(Np)^−Re s. Their product converges absolutely and locally uniformly and is nonzero there.
proofSketch: Apply artin-local-reciprocal-bound with θ=2^(−1−ε) and t=(Np)^−Re s. Since Np≥2, all local factors and their reciprocal partial products stay nonzero and their deviations from1 have a common summable majorant C_{d,ε}(Np)^−1−ε.

Prime ideals are a subset of the nonzero ideals; the full Dedekind series converges at1+ε. For the coefficient series, use the d-fold convolution majorant described in node160, whose ideal sum is ζ_K(1+ε)^d, including d=0.

ADS3 supplies the absolute/unordered product-to-series limit after these hypotheses. Summability of deviations gives a locally uniform product and summability for the reciprocal factors; the limit is nonzero. Dependence of the global bound on K is allowed, while the displayed local constant depends only on d,ε.

proofDependencies.title: Induction identity including ramification
proofDependencies.statement: For H⊆G and a complex finite-dimensional representation σ of H, with F=L^H, L_K(s,Ind_H^G σ)=L_F(s,σ) on Re s>1, including all ramified local factors.
proofSketch: Apply the ramified local induction polynomial identity at every prime p of K. The residue norm identity Nq=(Np)^f(q/p) matches every right-hand norm variable exactly.

Evaluate the finite local determinant identity at T=(Np)^−s, then rearrange the absolutely convergent prime products from node162. This is representation induction on H=Gal(L/F), including nonnormal F/K.

proofDependencies.title: Linear Artin factors are Hecke factors
proofDependencies.statement: For L/K finite Galois and a one-dimensional finite-order character χ:Gal(L/K)→C×, composition with the arithmetic global Artin map gives the canonical primitive finite-order Hecke character η. On Re s>1, the full Artin Euler series equals its full Hecke L-function. At p where χ is trivial on inertia both factors are (1−χ(Frob_p)(Np)^−s)^−1; otherwise both are1. The conductor and archimedean signs come from the same local/global reciprocity dictionary.
proofSketch: Compose χ with the existing globalArtinMap, using its principal-ideles triviality and local compatibility; obtain the existing GNF9 finite-order primitive character, with its real-place sign from CFT11.

CFT7 characterConductorExp and its unramified criterion identify local conductor exponent0 exactly with inertia-triviality. Compare the arithmetic Frobenius local value at those primes; at positive conductor exponent both local factors are1.
Evaluate absolutely convergent products and use the existing Hecke Euler comparison. Do not use an arbitrary imprimitive modulus to erase extra primes or invert the arithmetic Artin normalization.

proofDependencies.title: Nonnegative ray-character logarithmic coefficients
proofDependencies.statement: For a finite abelian ray-class quotient H and its full complex character group Ĥ, for h∈H and an integer k≥1, Σ_{χ∈Ĥ}χ(h^k) is #H if h^k=1 and 0 otherwise. On Re s>1 the contribution of an allowed prime ideal 𝔭 to log ∏_χL(s,χ) is Σ_{k≥1}(Σ_χχ([𝔭]^k))/k · N𝔭^(−ks). Thus these logarithmic coefficients are nonnegative after norm regrouping, with bad primes omitted consistently.
proofSketch: Use the actual finite abelian ray quotient and its complete dual: sum χ(h^k)=#H when h^k=1 and0 otherwise. This orthogonality is an explicit GNF9 supplier requirement, not an inference from the special Dirichlet-character theorem.
Choose the Euler logarithm that tends to0 as Re s→∞. Its prime-power expansion is absolutely locally uniformly convergent on Re s>1, includes1/k and may be interchanged with the finite character sum.

Regroup nonnegative real coefficients by the positive integer norm (with coefficient0 at norm0); ideals sharing the same norm are added. A common finite modulus removes the same bad prime set for every character, including the principal one.

proofDependencies.title: Nonreal Hecke characters are nonzero at one
proofDependencies.statement: For a finite-order ray character χ with χ≠χ̄, its canonical L(1,χ) is nonzero.
proofSketch: Match conjugation of the continued Hecke functions at real s=1; the distinct χ and χ̄ factors have the same positive zero order if either vanishes.

All nonprincipal factors are holomorphic at1 and the principal incomplete factor has exactly one pole of order1 (its deleted local polynomials are nonzero at1). Thus the full ray product would have total order≥1.
The existing ray-product Landau corollary prohibits a zero at1 and therefore prohibits that positive total order. This argument does not require Artin holomorphy.

proofDependencies.title: Positive quadratic auxiliary Euler factors
proofDependencies.statement: For a nonprincipal quadratic Hecke character χ, Ψ(s)=L(s,χ)ζ_K(s)/ζ_K(2s) has, on Re s>1, local factors (1+x)/(1−x) when χ(p)=1, 1 when χ(p)=−1, and1+x at omitted character primes, x=(Np)^−s. Hence its norm-regrouped Dirichlet coefficients are nonnegative.
proofSketch: At every p put x=(Np)^−s. The ζ_K(s)/ζ_K(2s) factor is1+x. Multiply by1/(1−χ(p)x), taking χ(p)=0 at character-conductor primes. This gives (1+x)/(1−x),1,1+x in the split/inert/conductor cases.

The respective power series have coefficients1+2Σ_{k≥1}x^k,1,1+x. Every coefficient is real nonnegative and the unit-ideal coefficient is1. Multiply finite products using unique ideal factorization, then pass to absolute convergence and sum the finite norm fibres.

This packet uses the full ζ_K quotient; the source instead deletes the common level primes in its principal L-functions. Retaining1+x at omitted character primes is the correct full-zeta generalization.

proofDependencies.title: Auxiliary holomorphy under vanishing at one
proofDependencies.statement: If L(1,χ)=0 for the preceding quadratic character, Ψ extends holomorphically to Re s>1/2. Indeed ζ_K(2s) is nonzero there because Re(2s)>1, and the numerator’s zero cancels ζ_K’s pole at1. At s=1/2, Ψ extends with a zero of order at least1.
proofSketch: L(s,χ) is entire for nonprincipal finite-order χ; ζ_K has only its simple pole at1. Under L(1,χ)=0 the numerator therefore extends holomorphically there.
For Re s>1/2 the denominator ζ_K(2s) is nonzero by its convergent Euler product, so the quotient is holomorphic.

The reciprocal of ζ_K(2s) has a simple zero at s=1/2 with leading coefficient2/Res_{u=1}ζ_K(u). The numerator is holomorphic at1/2, hence the quotient is holomorphic there and vanishes, with order≥1 unless it is locally identically zero. The original Euler product shows it is not identically zero. No nonzero numerator value or simple quotient zero is presumed.

proofDependencies.title: Landau contradiction for a quadratic character
proofDependencies.statement: For a nonprincipal quadratic Hecke character χ, L(1,χ)≠0. If it vanished, the nonnegative Dirichlet series of Ψ from node168 would have abscissa≤1/2 by ADS8 Landau and node169 holomorphy. For every real σ>1/2 its value would then satisfy Ψ(σ)≥1, while node169 gives lim_{σ↓1/2}Ψ(σ)=0, a contradiction. No convergence or sum identity at σ=1/2 is required.
proofSketch: The series converges for Re s>1, so its abscissa is not +∞. If its finite abscissa a were>1/2, Landau would force a singularity at the real point a, contradicting node169. An abscissa of −∞ already supplies all these real convergence points. Hence the abscissa is≤1/2.
For each real σ>1/2, use the canonical continued-series identity on the connected half-plane and nonnegative coefficients with unit coefficient1 to prove Ψ(σ)≥1.

Continuity of the holomorphic extension at1/2 gives its right limit0. For σ sufficiently close to1/2 this contradicts Ψ(σ)≥1. The proof never uses a boundary series sum or an unjustified boundary-convergence claim.

proofDependencies.title: Analytic root on a nonvanishing disc
proofDependencies.statement: Let D=Metric.ball(a,r)⊆C with r>0,F analytic on D and F(z)≠0 there,m∈N with m≥1,z₀∈D and w₀^m=F(z₀). There exists an analytic R on D with R(z)^m=F(z) for every z∈D and R(z₀)=w₀. Any analytic S with the same powers and value at z₀ equals R throughout D.
proofSketch: The nonempty open disc is simply connected. Apply the existing Complex.exists_continuousOn_eqOn_exp_comp to F and upgrade its continuous logarithm L to analytic using node122.
Put R₀=exp(L/m). Since R₀ never vanishes and R₀(z₀)^m=F(z₀), c=w₀/R₀(z₀) has c^m=1. Define R=c R₀; it has the desired power and value without assuming an arbitrary principal-root branch.

The quotient S/R is continuous and lies in the finite set of mth roots of unity. Connectedness of D makes it constant; its value1 at z₀ proves uniqueness. The finite-root/discrete-image adapter remains formal work, not a newly formalized canonical root carrier.

proofDependencies.title: Overlaps of boundary-centred discs
proofDependencies.statement: If two open complex discs centred on Re s=1 intersect, their intersection is connected and contains a point with Re s>1.
proofSketch: Each open disc is convex as a real subset of C; their intersection is convex, hence preconnected and connected when nonempty.
Take z in the intersection. If Re z>1 it is the required point. If Re z<1, use z′=2−conj z; centres on Re=1 make both distances unchanged and Re z′>1.
If Re z=1, choose a positive real shift smaller than min(r−|z−a|,q−|z−b|). The triangle inequality preserves both strict ball inequalities and puts the shifted point to the right.

proofDependencies.title: Dedekind completed-functional-equation comparison
proofDependencies.statement: For a number field K with absolute discriminant D_K, r₁ real places and r₂ conjugate pairs of complex places, let Γ_R(s)=π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2) and Γ_C(s)=2(2π)^(−s)Γ(s), the pinned Complex.Gammaℝ and Complex.Gammaℂ. The canonical continuation supplied by Tate has Λ_K(s)=|D_K|^(s/2)Γ_R(s)^r₁Γ_C(s)^r₂ζ_K^cont(s), and Λ_K(1−s)=Λ_K(s) as meromorphic functions. No equality of totalized values at poles is asserted.
proofSketch: Import AL.1 global Tate functional equation, archimedean local factors and unramified finite factors, using the standard trace additive character and its self-dual measure.

At finite places the inverse different supplies |D_K|^(s/2); the conductor of the trivial character is the unit ideal. Compare Tate’s local constants with the displayed pinned gamma convention; s-independent constants cancel from the functional equation.
Use the Dedekind convergence-half-plane comparison to identify the continuation. The measure/different adapter is recorded as an open gap, rather than supplied by the global integral equation alone.

proofDependencies.title: Triangle inequality for pretentious products
proofDependencies.statement: For |f_j(p)|,|g_j(p)|≤1, D(f₁f₂,g₁g₂;x)≤D(f₁,g₁;x)+D(f₂,g₂;x). If all g_j have unit modulus on the primes, this gives the usual triangle inequality for prime data.
proofSketch: Apply unit-disc-product-distance to z=f₁(p)conj(g₁(p)), w=f₂(p)conj(g₂(p)) for each prime p≤x.
Multiply by sqrt(1/p), sum the squares, and apply finite Cauchy–Schwarz to obtain the weighted Euclidean product triangle.
For D(f,h)≤D(f,g)+D(g,h), the intermediate g must have |g(p)|=1 so f(p)conj(g(p))g(p)conj(h(p))=f(p)conj(h(p)). Do not impose a zero diagonal on arbitrary unit-disc functions.

proofDependencies.title: Beurling zeta and Euler product
proofDependencies.statement: If Σ_n n^−σ (with generalized-integer multiplicities) converges for every real σ>1, then ζ_P(s)=Σ_n n^−s=∏_j(1−p_j^−s)^−1 on Re s>1, absolutely and locally uniformly. The convergence hypothesis is additional to the prime-system axioms.
proofSketch: Define ζ_P(s) by the summable exponent-vector series exp(−s log norm(a)); keep the additional summability assumption for every realσ>1. For the first M indexed primes, independent geometric summation gives the finite Euler product, with ratio p_j^(−s) of norm<1.

Exhaust all finite-support vectors with the first M indices. On a compact K⊂{Re s>1}, choose1<σ₀<inf_K Re s; norm(a)≥1 makes the summable norm(a)^−σ₀ series a uniform majorant. The finite-prime tails converge uniformly to the full series.

For a nonzero Euler product, additionally sum the logarithmic local factors using |p_j^(−s)|≤p_j^−σ₀ and the prime-index-to-vector injection. The normalized analytic logarithm is this convergent sum, not an arbitrary pointwise principal logarithm of ζ_P.

proofDependencies.title: Lerch compact convergence
proofDependencies.statement: On every compact subset of |z|<1, Re c>0, s∈C, the Φ series and each fixed derivative in z,s,c converge uniformly and absolutely.
proofSketch: For a compact subset choose0<r₀<r<1 with |z|≤r₀, Re c≥δ>0, and |s|,|c| bounded. The principal argument of n+c stays within(−π/2,π/2). Thus |exp(−sLog(n+c))|≤C(n+1)^B uniformly, after treating finitely many small n.

Each fixed mixed derivative contributes finitely many factors polynomial in n, shifted powers of n+c and powers of Log(n+c). Differentiating z^n directly treats z=0 correctly: its d-th derivative is0 for n<d and a falling factorial times z^(n−d) otherwise.

Absorb every fixed polynomial/logarithmic factor and the finite index shift into C r^n using r₀<r; use a summable geometric majorant for absolute, uniform convergence and joint termwise differentiation.

proofSketch: Separate n=0 and reindex n≥1 in the absolutely convergent series.

proofSketch: Differentiate termwise using compact uniform convergence.

proofDependencies.statement: On the initial domain, ∂_cΦ(z,s,c)=−sΦ(z,s+1,c), For an already constructed continuation the identity transports along the matching s+1 path by uniqueness.
proofSketch: Differentiate exp(−sLog(n+c)) termwise under compact convergence.

proofDependencies.title: Lerch integral representation
proofDependencies.statement: There exists a jointly holomorphic principal-sheet extension F(s,z,c) on Re s>0, Re c>0, z∈C\[1,∞), agreeing with the defining Φ series for |z|<1, such that F(s,z,c)=Γ(s)^−1∫_0^∞t^(s−1)exp(−ct)/(1−zexp(−t))dt. The integral is absolutely convergent; its formula is not asserted for the totalized series outside |z|<1.
proofSketch: For |z|<1, expand the denominator; the geometric bound and Re c>0 dominate the integral at∞ and Re s>0 dominates its origin. Apply the complex gamma integral and sum-integral interchange to identify the initial series.

On a compact subset outside the real cut[1,∞), the denominator has a positive lower bound on any fixed finite t interval, and is uniformly close to1 for large t. At t=0 it is bounded away from0 because z≠1. These bounds permit joint differentiation with integrable power/logarithmic majorants.

Define F by the absolutely convergent integral on this domain; joint holomorphy and agreement in the disc fix the principal sheet. The gamma integral for complex c and its parameter differentiation remain exact imported analytic adapters to verify.

proofDependencies.title: Monodromy around c=−n
proofDependencies.statement: On the principal Lerch-zeta germ ζ(s,a,c)=Φ(exp(2πia),s,c), a positive loop around c=−n (n≥0) changes the branch by (e^(−2πis)−1)e^(2πina)(c+n)^−s, with the same logarithm lift. Loops about positive integer c have zero monodromy.
proofSketch: Separate the n-th term by the shift formula; the remaining shifted tail is holomorphic around c=−n.
Continue (c+n)^−s once counterclockwise and subtract the original value.

proofDependencies.title: Monodromy around a=n
proofDependencies.statement: For the lifted principal Lerch-zeta branch, a positive loop around a=n∈Z changes it by −(2πi)^s Γ(s)^−1(a−n)^(s−1)e^(−2πic(a−n)), with (2πi)^s defined by log(2π)+iπ/2 and the continued logarithm of a−n. On the fundamental strip0<Re a<1, the logarithm of a−n is cut along the negative imaginary axis with argument in(−π/2,3π/2). Equivalently, for n≥1 replace(a−n)^(s−1) by exp(πi(s−1))(n−a)^(s−1), whose base has positive real part; for n≤0 use the principal logarithm of a−n.
proofSketch: Move the integral contour across the simple pole t=2πi(a−n), retaining the clockwise residue sign.
Continue the resulting residue term back to the principal polycylinder.

proofSketch: The finitely many indices |α_i|<1 contribute a fixed S, even when the minimum radius is small.

hypotheses: An indexed family α_i≠0 of complex numbers, with finitely many indices in every bounded disk; repeated indices represent multiplicity.

hypotheses: An indexed family α_i≠0 of complex numbers, with finitely many indices in every bounded disk; repeated indices represent multiplicity.

hypotheses: An indexed family α_i≠0 of complex numbers, with finitely many indices in every bounded disk; repeated indices represent multiplicity.

proofDependencies.title: Every xi zero lies in the open critical strip
proofDependencies.statement: For every complex ρ with ξ(ρ)=0,0<Re ρ<1.
proofSketch: For Re s≥1 and s!=1, the xi comparison has nonzero factors s,s−1,π^(−s/2),Gamma(s/2),zeta(s); pinned zeta nonvanishing includes the line Re s=1. At s=1, xi=1/2.
If Re s≤0, then Re(1−s)≥1 and xi(s)=xi(1−s) is nonzero by reflection.
Thus any zero has strict0<Re s<1, including exclusion of both boundary lines and all trivial zeta zeros.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform reciprocal-square zero weight
proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for every real t, Σ_(ξ(ρ)=0)mρ/(1+(t−Imρ)²) is summable and at most C log(2+|t|), with mρ=analyticOrderNatAt ξρ.
proofSketch: Evaluate the corrected Hadamard log derivative at s=2+it; the right-edge zeta series is bounded and the gamma term is O(log(2+|t|)), using compact continuity to include bounded t.
Write a=2−Reρ∈(1,2). Then Re(1/(2+it−ρ))=a/(a²+(t−Imρ)²)≥1/(4(1+(t−Imρ)²)). Also Re(1/ρ)>0.

The real parts of finite regularized sums are nonnegative. Their convergent limit therefore bounds the weighted positive sum; the same finite-sum comparison proves summability. Fixed Re B contributes only an absolute constant.
Absorb bounded t into log(2+|t|), which is always at least log2. This is the missing Exercise8.4.9 argument rather than an assumed Jensen centre bound.

proofDependencies.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ of conductor q≥1 and every real u, the nontrivial L-zero occurrences with u≤Imρ≤u+1 number at most C log(q(2+|u|)).
proofSketch: Use the pinned primitive completed L-function and its functional equation, retaining parity and conductor factor; gamma factors are nonzero on the open critical strip.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform finite Artin factor bound
proofDependencies.statement: For d∈N,0≤m≤d,0≤t≤θ<1 and α₁,…,α_m∈C with |α_j|=1, put A(z)=∏_{j=1}^m(1−α_j z). For |z|=t, A(z)≠0, |A(z)^−1|≤(1−θ)^−d and |A(z)^−1−1|≤d t(1−θ)^−d. The assertion includes d=m=0.
proofSketch: Each |1−α_j z|≥1−t≥1−θ>0, so every reciprocal factor exists and has norm≤(1−θ)^−1.

Telescope the reciprocal finite product: the jth term has one factor difference α_j z/(1−α_j z) and at most m−1 preceding factors. Each term is bounded by t(1−θ)^−m, and summing gives m t(1−θ)^−m≤d t(1−θ)^−d.

For a finite-order invariant-space automorphism, every characteristic root satisfies α^N=1 for a positive group exponent N, so |α|=1. The polynomial splits over C. This supplies the local factor hypotheses without choosing a new representation carrier.

proofDependencies.title: Ramified local Artin induction identity
proofDependencies.statement: For L/K finite Galois with group G,H≤G,F=L^H and σ a finite-dimensional complex representation of H, at every nonzero prime p of K, P_{p,Ind_H^Gσ}(T)=∏_{q|p in F}P_{q,σ}(T^{f(q/p)}). The right polynomials are defined from Gal(L/F)=H, their own inertia invariants and arithmetic Frobenius modulo inertia.
proofSketch: Fix P of L above p and its groups I⊲D. Match the primes q of F above p with H\G/D by NumberFieldArithmetic1.4, and use Mackey3a to split the induced representation restricted to D.

In each Mackey summand, take I-invariants. Frobenius permutes the inertia-orbit blocks in cycles of length f(q/p). The cycle return map is the relative Frobenius on the appropriate conjugated σ-invariant space, with independence only modulo inertia at a ramified prime.

The determinant of I−T times a cyclic block with return map A and cycle length f is det(I−T^f A). Multiply these blocks. The required ramified Frobenius/invariant-space and cyclic-block adapters are explicit open parts of the Artin gap; unramified automorphism equality is insufficient.

proofDependencies.title: Unit-disc product distance inequality
proofDependencies.statement: For complex z,w with |z|,|w|≤1, sqrt(1−Re(zw))≤sqrt(1−Re z)+sqrt(1−Re w).
proofSketch: Put a=1−Re z and b=1−Re w, so a,b≥0 and (Im z)²≤2a, (Im w)²≤2b by the unit-disc assumptions.
Then 1−Re(zw)=a+b−ab+(Im z)(Im w)≤a+b+2sqrt(ab)=(sqrt a+sqrt b)². Both sides are nonnegative, so take square roots. This proves the extension from the unit circle without assuming it.

proofDependencies.title: Finite-prime smooth Dirichlet series
proofDependencies.statement: For y≥2 and σ>0, the nonnegative real series ∑_{n≥1, n y-smooth}n^(−σ) is summable and equals ∏_{p≤y}(1−p^(−σ))^(−1). This is a finite-prime identity valid for every positive σ, even σ≤1.
proofSketch: Use Nat.equivProdNatFactoredNumbers inductively on the finite set of primes≤y to index smooth positive integers by their independent nonnegative prime exponents.
Each p≥2 has0<p^(−σ)<1. Its geometric series is summable; finite products/Tonelli and rpow multiplication factor the sum. The zero integer is excluded by the existing carrier.
Identify the finite prime set with primes strictly below floor y+1. No infinite-prime Euler product on Re s>1 is substituted for this stronger finite-prime statement.

proofDependencies.title: Harmonic sum remainder

proofSketch: Unfold the two pinned Euler-sequence inequalities at N>0; subtract to trap H_N−log N−γ between0 and log(N+1)−log N.
Use log(N+1)−log N=log(1+1/N) and the pinned positive-real log inequality. No new Euler constant is defined.

proofDependencies.title: Divisor hyperbola identity
proofDependencies.statement: For real x≥1 and M=floor(sqrt x), Σ_{1≤n≤floor x}τ(n)+M²=2Σ_{1≤a≤M}floor(x/a). The equality is exact, including x at a perfect square.
proofSketch: Count positive ordered pairs(a,b) with ab≤x. A pair has a≤M or b≤M because (M+1)²>x.
Transpose to equate the two strips; their intersection is precisely1≤a,b≤M, containing M² pairs. Regroup pairs by ab and use the existing divisor carrier.

proofDependencies.title: Beurling counting growth from summability
proofDependencies.statement: For a Beurling system P, real σ>0 and S=Σ_a norm(a)^−σ with summable nonnegative summands, N(x)≤S x^σ for x≥1, and π_P(x)≤N(x). Thus convergence for every σ>1 gives N(x),π_P(x)=O_ε(x^(1+ε)) for every ε>0.
proofSketch: Each counted vector satisfies1≤x^σ norm(a)^−σ. Bound its finite sum by the full summable nonnegative sum.
Map each counted prime index injectively to its unit exponent vector. Repeated equal real primes remain distinct vectors.

proofDependencies.title: Beurling higher-prime-power correction
proofDependencies.statement: For x≥1, J=floor(log x/log p₁) and Π_P(x)=Σ_{1≤j≤J}π_P(x^(1/j))/j, all later terms are0. For x≥p₁, 0≤Π_P(x)−π_P(x)≤π_P(sqrt x)+π_P(x^(1/3))log x/log p₁. Under convergence for every σ>1, the difference is O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for every ε>0.
proofSketch: Use p₁>1 to bound j for any prime power≤x. Isolate j=1 and j=2; for3≤j≤J use x^(1/j)≤x^(1/3) and bound1/j≤1.
Apply the counting-growth lemma at exponent1+η with0<η<2ε. Absorb the logarithm in the strictly smaller exponent for the j≥3 contribution. The finite low-x range changes only the constant.

proofDependencies.title: Lerch z-loop monodromy and shifts
proofDependencies.statement: On D={s∈C,z∈C\[0,∞),0<Re c<1}, choose Log z with 0<Im Log z<2π and a=Log z/(2πi). Put f_p=e^(2πipc)z^−c(a−p)^(s−1) for p≤0, and f_p=e^(πi(s−1))e^(2πipc)z^−c(p−a)^(s−1) for p≥1, using principal logarithms of the positive-real-part bases. For the source upper-connector based loops Z₀,Z₁ about 0,1, the principal germ has M_Z₀Φ=0 and M_Z₁Φ=−(2πi)^s f₀/Γ(s). The residue functions analytically continue to the universal cover, and continuation along Z₀^k sends f_p to f_(p−k); positive continuation along Z₁^k multiplies f₀ by e^(2πiks) and fixes f_p for p≠0; c loops fix every f_p. This corrects the published (3.28), as recorded in E29. The vanishing Z₀ identity for Φ concerns its principal germ, not invariance on every sheet.
proofSketch: Lift Z₀ by the exponential cover to a path from a=1/2 to3/2 in the upper half-plane; the initial Fourier series is periodic there, so Φ has zero Z₀ monodromy. Z₁ lifts to the a=0 based loop, giving the existing a-monodromy residue.

The continued Log z increases by 2πik along Z₀^k. Its factor z^−c contributes e^(−2πikc); combined with e^(2πipc) this is the phase in f_(p−k). Track the cut of a−p using the stated positive-real-part bases, including a sign change of p−k. The principal-germ identities then have unique analytic continuations on the universal cover.

The Z₁ lift winds positively once around a=0, while its logarithm lift has no increment around z=0. Thus a^(s−1) gains e^(2πis) for p=0. For p≠0, the corresponding a−p factor has zero winding. Repetition gives e^(2πiks). These principal-germ relations extend analytically on the connected universal cover. The descent argument must use this corrected diagonal action, not published (3.28).

proofDependencies.title: Small-prime divisor logarithm
proofDependencies.statement: For a natural n≥2 and real y≥2, Σ_{p∈primeFactors(n), p≤y} log(v_p(n)+1) ≤ y log(1+log n/log 2).
hypotheses: The ranges and positivity assumptions are explicit in the statement.
proofSketch: For each p dividing n, p≥2 and p^v_p(n) divides n. Monotonicity of log and log_pow give v_p(n)≤log n/log 2.
Bound each nonnegative summand by log(1+log n/log 2). There are at most floor y distinct positive integers ≤y; cast this cardinality bound to R and multiply.

proofDependencies.title: Large-prime divisor logarithm
proofDependencies.statement: For a natural n≥2 and real y>1, Σ_{p∈primeFactors(n), y<p} log(v_p(n)+1) ≤ (log 2)log n/log y.
hypotheses: The ranges and positivity assumptions are explicit in the statement.
proofSketch: Induction on a gives a+1≤2^a, hence log(a+1)≤a log 2.

The factorization identity and log_prod/log_pow give Σ_{p|n}v_p(n)log p=log n. All terms are nonnegative. On the large-prime part, log y Σ v_p(n)≤log n; divide by the positive log y and multiply by log 2.

proofDependencies.title: Vanishing small-prime contribution
proofDependencies.statement: For real 0<δ<1 and η>0 there is L₀≥e such that for every real L≥L₀, L^(1−δ)log(1+L/log 2) ≤ η L/log L.
hypotheses: The ranges and positivity assumptions are explicit in the statement.
proofSketch: For large L, log(1+L/log 2)≤C log L for an absolute C, by monotonicity and splitting off a fixed multiplicative constant.
After dividing by the positive L/log L, the ratio is at most C(log L)^2/L^δ. The pinned isLittleO_log_rpow_rpow_atTop with r=2 and s=δ makes this eventually at most η. Increase the threshold to e.

proofDependencies.statement: For g∈axbRat and b∈Q, g translation(b) g⁻¹=translation(b/diagEntry(g)).
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Use the explicit inverse matrix and multiply all three factors. The upper-right entry is b/a and the diagonal is 1.

proofDependencies.title: Double-coset coordinate bijection
proofDependencies.statement: For positive coprime n,m, b↦class([1,b/m;0,n/m]) factors through Q/Z. The resulting map from triples (n,m,γ), gcd(n,m)=1, to axbInt\axbRat/axbInt is bijective. Equality of two representatives with fixed n,m is exactly equality of γ in Q/Z.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Reduce the positive rational diagonal uniquely to n/m in lowest terms. Left and right integral translations change b by Z+(n/m)Z=(1/m)Z. Multiplication by m identifies the remaining coordinate with Q/Z and proves injectivity and surjectivity.

proofDependencies.title: Double cosets of the ax+b pair and their degrees
proofDependencies.statement: The left-coset degree of an ax+b double coset X is den(cosetEntry X), where cosetEntry is its positive rational diagonal value.
hypotheses: None.
proofSketch: Left multiplication by [1 k; 0 1] sends [1 b; 0 a] to [1, b + ka; 0, a] and right multiplication by [1 j; 0 1] sends it to [1, b + j; 0, a]; so the double coset is b mod ℤ + aℤ = (1/m)ℤ, with a unchanged.
HeckeCoset.degree_eq_relIndex: the degree is the index of P⁺_ℤ ∩ g P⁺_ℤ g⁻¹ in P⁺_ℤ, which is m by B.9/ax-plus-b-hecke-triple; the inverse double coset has (2,2) entry 1/a = m/n, so its degree is n.

proofDependencies.title: Rational and isometric generator conventions
proofDependencies.statement: Over C put μ_n=n^(−1/2)x_n. Then μ_n*=n^(−1/2)x′_n, μ_n*μ_n=1, μ_n μ_n*=(1/n)Σnδ=0 eδ, and μ_n eγ μ_n*=(1/n)Σnδ=γ eδ. All positive scalar square roots use the real branch.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Replace x by sqrt(n) times mu in the left-inverse and preimage-sum identities. Positivity of n fixes the square-root branch and conjugation leaves that scalar unchanged.

proofDependencies.title: Isometries and phase unitaries on l²(N+)
proofDependencies.statement: S_n ε_k=ε_nk is a linear isometry; S_n* ε_k is ε_(k/n) if n divides k, and 0 otherwise. D_(u,γ)ε_k=ζ_(kuγ)ε_k is unitary. Their relations realize μ_n and eγ, giving the bounded regular representation.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Compute inner products on finitely supported basis vectors. Multiplication by n is injective, so the shift preserves the squared norm; the diagonal multipliers have modulus one. Extend these maps by continuity and calculate their adjoints on the basis.

proofDependencies.title: Algebraic GNS generator estimates
proofDependencies.statement: For every positive normalized algebraic functional φ, the GNS quotient seminorm obeys ‖μ_n[a]‖φ=‖[a]‖φ, ‖eγ[a]‖φ=‖[a]‖φ and ‖μ_n*[a]‖φ≤‖[a]‖φ. The last inequality follows from 1−μ_n μ_n* being a self-adjoint projection, hence a square.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Apply the algebraic relations inside φ(a*μ_n*μ_n a) and φ(a*eγ*eγ a).
Use φ(a*(1−μ_n μ_n*)a)≥0 because the middle projection equals its own square.
Bound every finite generator word, so left multiplication descends to bounded operators on the Hilbert completion.

proofDependencies.title: Inverse double-coset degree
proofDependencies.statement: The degree of X⁻¹ is num(cosetEntry X), a positive integer. Thus L(X)/R(X)=cosetEntry(X)⁻¹. The numerator is its absolute natural numerator, since the diagonal value is positive.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Invert the reduced diagonal n/m, which exchanges n and m. Apply the degree formula to the inverse class, then divide the two positive integer degrees.

proofDependencies.title: Finite convolution row and column counts
proofDependencies.statement: On Q=axbRat/axbInt use K_X(gH,hH)=1_X(g⁻¹h). Every row has L(X) nonzero entries and every column R(X)=L(X⁻¹). These counts are constant on quotient representatives.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Fix one quotient variable and identify the nonzero kernel entries with the appropriate left-coset decomposition of X. Interchanging variables replaces X by its inverse. Translation invariance proves independence of quotient representatives.

proofDependencies.title: Schur estimate for one double coset
proofDependencies.statement: For finitely supported ξ on Q, ‖K_X ξ‖₂²≤L(X)R(X)‖ξ‖₂². Consequently K_X extends uniquely to l²(Q) with operator norm≤sqrt(L(X)R(X)).

Sum the rows; every input entry occurs R times.
Extend on the dense finite-support subspace with this exact bound.

proofDependencies.statement: For finite-support f, its left convolution on l²(Q) satisfies ‖λ(f)‖≤ΣX∈supp f |f(X)|sqrt(L(X)R(X)). This gives the bounded algebra homomorphism λ; no C*-closure is used to obtain the estimate.
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

Use the triangle inequality and the preceding operator bound.
Kernel convolution on finite-support vectors proves multiplicativity; extend by density.

proofDependencies.title: Coefficient recovery and faithfulness
proofDependencies.statement: For δ_H the unit vector at the identity coset, (λ(f)δ_H)(gH)=f(class(g⁻¹)). Thus λ(f)=0 implies f=0. Faithfulness precedes the completion.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Evaluate the operator on the identity-coset unit vector. Only the identity input coordinate survives, recovering the coefficient at the inverse class. Vanishing of the operator therefore annihilates every coefficient.

proofDependencies.title: Universal C*-norm of the BC core
proofDependencies.statement: The supremum of ‖π(f)‖ over unital star representations of the complex BC core is finite: if f=Σc_(n,m,γ)μ_n eγ μ_m*, it is at most Σ|c_(n,m,γ)|. It is a norm, because λ is faithful. Its completion has the universal property for these representations.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Express each element in the independent normalized monomial basis. Every bounded star representation sends these monomials to contractions, giving the coefficient l1 bound. The faithful left-regular representation separates zero; the standard completion then has the stated representation property. The general completion theorem is the OP2-universal supplier contract.

proofDependencies.title: Division endomorphisms on the existing profinite ring
proofDependencies.statement: On C(Ẑ), α_n(f)(x)=f(x/n) for x∈nẐ and 0 elsewhere. This is an injective star endomorphism, α_nα_m=α_nm, and α_n(1)=1_(nẐ). Import Ẑ, its p-adic product and unit subgroup from ProfiniteArithmetic; do not reconstruct these objects.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Use that n times the integral adeles is compact open. Extension by zero of the pullback is continuous; direct evaluation proves star, product and composition identities. Surjectivity onto the corner and injectivity follow by evaluating on n times each integral adele.

proofDependencies.title: Minimal finite-adele dilation
proofDependencies.statement: Extension by zero i:C(Ẑ)→C0(A_f) is injective. The action β_q f(x)=f(q⁻¹x) extends α_n, and ⋃n β_(1/n)(i(C(Ẑ))) is dense in C0(A_f). Hence this is the minimal automorphic dilation.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Use the compact-open exhaustion of finite adeles by n^(-1) times the integral adeles. Functions supported on each such compact open set come from the corresponding translated integral function algebra. Compactly supported functions are dense in C0, proving minimality.

proofDependencies.title: BC algebra as a full crossed-product corner
proofDependencies.statement: Let B=C0(A_f)⋊Q_+×, for β_q f(x)=f(q⁻¹x), and p=1_Ẑ. The universal BC completion is star isomorphic to pBp, sending μ_n to U_n p and eγ to its additive-character function on Ẑ. The projection p is full: the closed span of BpB is B.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Check the BC relations on U_n p and characters; use the algebraic lift.
Dilate each covariant isometric representation to a unitary rational representation, as Lemma 2.1.3, pp.6–7; compression establishes the universal norm equality.
The translates (1/n)Ẑ exhaust A_f, so the ideal generated by p contains a dense set of compactly supported functions and their rational translates.

proofDependencies.title: Universal and reduced BC norms agree
proofDependencies.statement: Q_+× is abelian, hence amenable; its full and reduced crossed-product norms on C0(A_f) agree. The full-corner identification and the regular Hecke representation therefore give ‖f‖univ=‖λ(f)‖ for every f in the BC core.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Apply the amenable crossed-product theorem from OP2-dilation-corner to the abelian positive rational group. Transport its norm equality through the full-corner maps and identify the reduced representation with the faithful Hecke representation.

proofDependencies.title: Absolute Gibbs diagonal summability
proofDependencies.statement: For β>1 and bounded a∈C_Q, |⟨ε_k,π_u(a)ε_k⟩|≤‖a‖ and Σk k^(−β)<∞. Thus the diagonal Gibbs sum converges absolutely, defines a functional of norm≤1 after division by ζ(β), and is positive on squares.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Bound every diagonal coefficient by the operator norm and dominate the sum by zeta(beta). Each coefficient on a star square is a squared vector norm; normalization on 1 and positivity give the norm-one state.

proofDependencies.title: Convolution preserves the adjoint
proofDependencies.statement: For f in the complex Hecke algebra, λ(f*)=λ(f)*, since K_(f*)(gH,hH)=conj K_f(hH,gH). Both sides are bounded, so equality on finite-support vectors suffices.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Reverse the two quotient variables in the finite-support kernel and conjugate the coefficients. Inner products on finite-support vectors prove the adjoint equality; boundedness extends it to the Hilbert space.

proofDependencies.title: Dense isometric core embedding
proofDependencies.statement: The map ι:BCHecke C→C_Q is an injective star algebra homomorphism with dense range and ‖ι(f)‖=‖λ(f)‖. C_Q has the inherited unital C*-algebra structure of its closed star subalgebra of bounded operators.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Embed the faithful core into the operator-norm closure. Multiplication, involution and norm are inherited from bounded operators, while density is the closure property and injectivity is coefficient recovery.

proofDependencies.title: Entire Hecke orbit maps
proofDependencies.statement: For each f in the finite-support Hecke core, z↦ι(σ_z f) is an entire C_Q-valued map, supported on the same finite set of double cosets. For real t it is implemented in λ by the diagonal unitary with weights a(g)^(−it).
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: On the support it is a finite sum of exponentials z↦exp(iz log a(X)) times fixed vectors.
For the specified kernel use U_t(gH)=a(g)^(−it); conjugation multiplies K_f by a(g⁻¹h)^(it).

proofDependencies.title: Gibbs strip correlations
proofDependencies.statement: For β>1 and core a,b, the Gibbs correlation Σk ζ(β)⁻¹k^(−β)⟨ε_k,π_u(a σ_z b)ε_k⟩ converges locally uniformly on C and uniformly on each closed real strip of bounded imaginary height. On the KMS strip 0≤Imz≤β it has the required two boundary values; finite normal-form reindexing supplies the upper boundary.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Finite support of a,b bounds all complex-time coefficients on each bounded imaginary strip. Dominate the diagonal sum by C k^(−β).
Check the boundary identity on normal forms by the divisibility formula and change k to nk; the factor n^(−β) is exactly the imaginary-time scalar.
Extend bilinearly to the core and then by the core strip equivalence.

proofDependencies.title: Positive Hecke states extend boundedly
proofDependencies.statement: Every normalized positive complex-linear φ on the BC core has |φ(f)|≤‖λ(f)‖, and therefore a unique norm-one positive continuous extension to C_Q. Its restriction is φ; extensions agree by core density.
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.
proofSketch: Use the cyclic unit vector in the bounded algebraic GNS representation to get |φ(f)|≤‖f‖univ.
Replace the universal norm by the regular norm and extend continuously.
Approximate a completed square by core squares to preserve positivity.

proofDependencies.title: Uniform correlation bound on the closed strip
proofDependencies.statement: Let φ be a completed state satisfying the core KMS identity at β>0. For core a,b, F(z)=φ(ι(a σ_z b)) is entire and bounded on 0≤Imz≤β. The two boundary bounds are≤‖ι(a)‖‖ι(b)‖; the three-lines principle gives the same bound throughout the strip.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Finite spectral support bounds F on each closed strip, before invoking three-lines.
The KMS identity identifies the upper boundary with φ(σ_t(b)a); both real automorphism norms are unchanged.
Apply the bounded-strip maximum principle.

proofDependencies.title: Extending real dynamics to the C*-completion
proofDependencies.statement: The real σt are isometric star automorphisms in the left representation and extend to a point-norm-continuous automorphism group on C_Q. The complex σz is retained only on the entire dense Hecke algebra.
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.
proofSketch: Implement real σt by diagonal unitaries from the dilation character.
Extend the norm-preserving map and inverse to the closure.
Approximate by finite Hecke sums to prove point-norm continuity.

proofDependencies.title: Point-norm continuous completed dynamics
proofDependencies.statement: For every a∈C_Q, t↦σ_t(a) is continuous. Approximate a in norm by a core element, whose orbit is a finite exponential sum, and use the isometry of every σ_t to bound both approximation errors.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: For each core element the orbit is a finite sum of scalar exponentials. Approximate an arbitrary completed element in norm by a core element and bound the two approximation terms using the isometric dynamics.

proofDependencies.title: The analytic core and the strip KMS condition
proofDependencies.statement: For β>0 a completed state is KMSβ exactly when its restriction to the dense Hecke core satisfies IsKMS β. In the core-to-strip direction, approximate both completed arguments by core arguments; the uniform strip estimate makes their correlation functions Cauchy uniformly on the closed strip.
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.
proofSketch: Restrict a bounded strip correlation and use uniqueness against the entire core orbit to evaluate the upper boundary.
For the converse take norm approximations a_j,b_j in the core. The bound on differences gives uniform convergence on the full closed strip.
Locally uniform limits remain holomorphic, and the limits have the required two boundary values.

locators.locator: Chapter 3, Definition 3.6 and entire-element condition (3.17), pp.446–447; the converse analytic-core theorem is an additional source gap

proofDependencies.title: Finite-prime orbit projection
proofDependencies.statement: For a finite prime set A, NA is its generated multiplicative monoid and WA={x∈Ẑ:xp∈Zp× for p∈A}. On WA the projection to NA-invariant functions is PAf(x)=ζA(β)^(−1)Σn∈NA n^(−β)f(nx), extended along NA-orbits, where ζA(β)=∏p∈A(1−p^(−β))^(−1).
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.
proofSketch: Decompose Ẑ into disjoint nWA for n∈NA up to the measure-zero zero-coordinate set.
Use μβ(nE)=n^(−β)μβ(E).
