proofDependencies.statement: For a countable essentially free ergodic nonsingular action on a standard sigma-finite measure space, RatioSet=[0,∞) implies its group-measure factor has type III1; equivalently its flow of weights is trivial. This is the operator classification input, distinct from the arithmetic ratio witnesses.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Apply OP2-factor to the established essentially free ergodic action and its full nonnegative ratio set. The theorem identifies the Connes type from that measured ratio invariant; no arithmetic witness replaces this classification input.

proofDependencies.title: A nonzero full corner preserves factor type
proofDependencies.statement: The GNS algebra of the diagonal-expectation KMS state is p(L∞(A_f,μβ)⋊Q+×)p, where p=1Ẑ and p≠0. A nonzero corner of a type III1 factor is again type III1. The C*-full corner identification and the von Neumann compression identification are separate requirements.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Use the expectation-measure construction to identify the completed state GNS algebra with the integral projection compression of the group-measure factor. Normalization makes that projection nonzero. Apply OP2-factor nonzero-corner type invariance.

proofDependencies.title: The Gibbs limit and its uniform tail bound
proofDependencies.statement: For β→∞ the Gibbs states converge weakly to the ε1 vector state, uniformly on each fixed norm-bounded observable set: the difference is at most2||a||(ζ(β)−1)/ζ(β), which tends to0. This supplies completed KMS∞ states.
hypotheses: The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.
proofSketch: Separate k=1 from the Gibbs diagonal sum.
Bound every matrix coefficient by||a||.
Use ζ(β)−1→0 and the normalization difference.

locators.locator: Chapter 3, (3.140)–(3.142), pp.475–476; weak Gibbs limit is the stated elementary consequence

proofDependencies.title: Polynomial growth of cleared double series
proofDependencies.statement: For each compact real rectangle I×J there exist C,N>0 with |Eij(s,w)|≤C(1+|Ims|)^N(1+|Imw|)^N whenever Res∈I,Rew∈J. Here Eij is the entire cleared continuation.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Obtain polynomial bounds on every component of the R6 shell from the compact-uniform primitive moment and uniform Gamma ratio. Normalize by (3+s)^M(3+w)^M on a real-part ball and use bounded reciprocal tube extension. Translate the ball under the functional system to cover the requested rectangle.

proofDependencies.title: Cubic residue at one
proofDependencies.statement: With AF=ζF(2)ρF/2^(r1+r2+1), residue at 1 is AF(1+3^(−rα−r2)). Here ρF is the residue of ζF at 1 and rα counts split real cubic factors.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Compare the ordinary-series normalization with the adelic residue at u=2, including the factor one-half under u=2s and all local lattice masses. Insert the number-field zeta residue and sum the real signature weights, giving AF times the displayed factor.

proofDependencies.title: Cubic secondary residue
proofDependencies.statement: With BF=3^(r1+r2/2)ζF(1/3)ρF/[6·2^(r1+r2)D^(1/2)]·[Γ(1/3)^3/(2π)]^n, residue at 5/6 is BF·3^(−rα/2). All discriminants are absolute norms.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Compare the adelic Sigma1 residue at u=5/3 with the arithmetic parameter s=5/6. Evaluate the archimedean orbital integrals and finite discriminant factors in the fixed self-dual normalization; their product is BF and the remaining signature weight is 3^(-r_alpha/2).

locators.locator: Definition before Proposition 3.7 and Proposition 3.7(2), p.12

proofDependencies.title: KMS-infinity limits are ground states
proofDependencies.statement: For a unital C*-system with point-norm continuous dynamics, each KMS∞ state is a ground state. On every finite upper strip the KMSβ correlation functions, for sufficiently large β, are bounded by ‖a‖‖b‖; use normal families and boundary convergence.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Take beta tending to infinity along the weak state limit. On each fixed upper strip the correlation functions have a common norm bound once beta exceeds its height. A diagonal normal-family limit is analytic on the upper half-plane and has the required boundary values.

proofDependencies.title: Ground and KMS-infinity differ for trivial dynamics
proofDependencies.statement: For M₂(C) with σ_t=id, every state is a ground state, while every KMSβ state is tracial and every KMS∞ state is tracial. The vector state a↦a₀₀ is ground and is not KMS∞: on matrix units it gives φ(E₀₁E₁₀)=1 and φ(E₁₀E₀₁)=0.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: With trivial dynamics every correlation function is constant and bounded on the upper half-plane. The KMS boundary condition reduces to the trace identity and traces form a weakly closed set. Evaluate the two matrix-unit products in the vector state to exclude that identity.

proofDependencies.title: Normalize the local scaling density
proofDependencies.statement: For β>0 and every integer k, μβ,p({ordp x=k})=(1−p^(−β))p^(−kβ). Summing k≥0 gives μβ,p(Zp)=1; the singleton 0 has mass 0. Multiplication by p^j scales measurable masses by p^(−jβ).
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Integrate the radial density on each additive-Haar shell. Its Haar mass is (1-p^(-1))p^(-k), so the normalization constant yields (1-p^(-beta))p^(-k beta). Sum the nonnegative shells and apply a change of variables for dilation by p^j.

proofDependencies.title: Arithmetic generation after adjoining isometries
proofDependencies.statement: The Q-algebra generated by all first functions and μn,μn* equals the normalized arithmetic form A1,Q spanned by μn e(a) μm*. The comparison to Q-valued Hecke functions is through σ−i/2 and is not a star-algebra identification.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Recover every torsion generator from the first functions by the prime-level induction. The eight relations reduce every word with isometries and adjoints to the normalized arithmetic monomial span. The imaginary-time comparison records which rational form this is.

locators.locator: Ch.3, Theorem 3.30, pp.467–470; rational-form convention pp.460–462

proofDependencies.title: Complexification of the arithmetic form
proofDependencies.statement: The scalar-extension map C⊗Q A1,Q→H_C is an algebra isomorphism sending 1⊗μn e(a) μm* to the normalized complex normal form. Its image is dense in the completed BC algebra. Rational Hecke and arithmetic forms remain distinct subalgebras until the specified imaginary-time comparison.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Use linear independence and spanning of normalized complex normal forms to prove bijectivity of scalar extension.
Use density of the Hecke core in its operator-norm completion.

locators.locator: Ch.3, Theorem 3.30 and surrounding discussion, pp.460–470

proofDependencies.title: Spectral continuation output
proofDependencies.statement: The heat-asymptotic contract yields actual positive and shifted meromorphic functions, regular at z=0, agreeing with their convergent series on Rez>1. It also yields an analytic function F=(z−1)ζ+(z) near 1. These are the fields of SpectralContinuation; existence follows from the Mellin subtraction chain, not from an arbitrary function-valued placeholder.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement.
proofSketch: Assemble the normally convergent right-half-plane series, the subtracted Mellin germs and regularity at zero into actual continuation functions. Their overlapping germs agree by the identity theorem. The pole-cleared germ near one is the data used in the genus-one prefactor.

readerConventions.chebyshev: ψ(x) and θ(x) are Mathlib’s Chebyshev.psi and Chebyshev.theta with inclusive cutoff ⌊x⌋; θ(x;a,q) restricts θ to primes p ≡ a mod q with gcd(a,q) = 1. ψ₀ in explicit formulas gives half weight to x when x is a prime power.
readerConventions.characters: Dirichlet characters are Mathlib DirichletCharacter ℂ N; L(s,χ) is DirichletCharacter.LFunction, which for imprimitive χ keeps the missing Euler factors. Conductor-uniform statements use the conductor of the primitive character, never the modulus.
readerConventions.zeros: Zeros are counted with analytic multiplicity (analyticOrderNatAt). Nontrivial zeros of ζ are the zeros of the entire Riemann xi function; trivial zeros and the junk value of riemannZeta at 1 are excluded explicitly.
readerConventions.exceptionalZero: An exceptional zero is a real zero β of L(s,χ), χ primitive real nonprincipal of conductor N > 1, with 1 − c/log N < β < 1 for a stated c; ineffective constants (Siegel) are labelled as such.
readerConventions.perron: Perron inversion is ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 6: the finite-height kernel at x = 1 is π⁻¹ arctan(T/c), and 1/2 is only its limit.
readerConventions.hurwitzLerch: Mathlib’s Hurwitz zeta takes a parameter in UnitAddCircle; the complex-parameter Hurwitz series is a separate object here. With Φ(z,s,a) = Σ_{n≥0} zⁿ (n+a)^{−s}, Mathlib’s exponential zeta is z·Φ(z,s,1).
readerConventions.conditional: RH, GRH, the extended RH, Artin holomorphy and the moment conjecture are Prop-valued predicates used only as hypotheses of conditional theorems; no unconditional target depends on them.
readerConventions.gamma: Real and complex gamma factors are Mathlib Complex.Gammaℝ s = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Complex.Gammaℂ s = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s).
